clue.text: Singer, perhaps from Spain, into big-band music, its leader adding a sparkle, they say

indicators.note: the Spanish letter is placed into the big-band style, splitting it

parts.note: swing is the big-band jazz style of the 1930s and 40s
E is the international vehicle code for Spain

indicators.note: the leading letter of the word music, which 'its' points back to
signals that the phrase must be pronounced rather than spelt

parts.note: a sheen is a sparkle or gloss; the same sound ends the second word

explanation.surface: A singer from Spain joins a big band and adds some sparkle to the music.
explanation.walkthrough: Singer is the famous maker of sewing machines, so the capital misleads. 'into' signals the container, 'its leader' takes the first letter of music, and 'they say' marks the sound of a word for sparkle.
explanation.definitionFit: Singer is a well-known brand of domestic stitching appliance, so a Singer is an example of one.

clue.text: One sings a note softly, Queen taking one's place

parts.note: so (or soh) is the fifth note of the sol-fa scale

indicators.note: the queen's letter goes where the letter for one stood, replacing it

parts.note: piano is the musical direction meaning softly
R, for Regina, is the usual abbreviation for a queen

explanation.surface: A singer holds a quiet note while the Queen steps in for someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'softly' is the musical term piano; 'taking one's place' means R (Regina) replaces I, the Roman one.
explanation.definitionFit: A soprano is the highest female voice, so she is a person who sings.

clue.text: Origins of wassailing at inn swelling the belly

indicators.note: origins are beginnings, so take the opening letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: Drinking at the pub during wassail makes one's stomach swell.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Origins of' runs across five words, including 'swelling' and 'the', which look like part of the definition. Wassailing is the old custom of drinking toasts and carol-singing at Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: The belly is the middle of the body, loosely the part around the midriff, so it stands for it.

clue.text: Nil — no contest

definitions.meaning: nil means nothing at all, not the smallest piece
taken literally, no fight or scrap took place

explanation.surface: A sports report: nil, so it was a walkover.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means 'nothing whatever', matching nil; read literally a scrap is a fight, so it also means no contest.

clue.text: Sing softly, lazily, steamily

parts.note: to hum is to sing quietly with closed lips
idly means in a lazy way

explanation.surface: Someone croons quietly and languidly in a steamy room.
explanation.definitionFit: Steamy air is damp and close, so acting steamily is acting in a muggy, moist way.

clue.text: Falsetto? Oh, of course: like a bat out of hell!

definitions.text: course: like a bat out of hell

parts.note: read as 'False tto oh of': the word false, split off the front of the singing term, tells you to rearrange the letters that follow it

explanation.surface: A singer's falsetto prompts a cry of 'of course!' and a frantic dash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Falsetto' does two jobs as a split word: its front half, false, is the anagram signal and its tail joins the next two words as the letters to rearrange. 'course' is the verb, to run.
explanation.definitionFit: To hotfoot it is to rush, so it means to run at speed, the way a bat out of hell is said to fly.

clue.text: Apes dress top-down

indicators.note: in this down entry the top letter is moved down to the bottom

parts.note: a smock is a loose dress

explanation.surface: Monkeys dress from the top downwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top-down' moves the first letter of SMOCK to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To ape someone is to imitate them, often mockingly, which is a synonym for ridicule by copying.

clue.text: Sad ballad (woe!) to produce a hit

indicators.note: a sad state is a sorry, broken one, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A mournful ballad full of woe nevertheless becomes a chart success.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sad' rearranges BALLAD and WOE; 'hit' suggests a chart success, not a punch.
explanation.definitionFit: To deal a blow is to strike someone, so it means landing a hit.

clue.text: Constant talking puts treaty under strain

indicators.note: letters under strain are pulled out of shape, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Endless chatter puts a treaty under pressure.
explanation.definitionFit: Yatter is informal for incessant chatter, the same as constant talking.

clue.text: Tenor with no depth on top note for cash

indicators.note: in a down entry the first piece sits above the second
says the depth abbreviation is to be removed from the word

parts.note: the tenor of something is its general mood
lah is the sixth note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: A tenor with a thin voice tops a note for money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tenor' looks like the singer but is the general mood of something. 'with no' drops D; 'on top' places the result above the note in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Moolah is a slang word for money, so it means cash.

clue.text: Shows clue to news

definitions.meaning: to show is to indicate or draw attention to
the letters of news are the compass points spelled out: north, east, west, south

explanation.surface: A television schedule: programmes that hint at the news.
explanation.definitionFit: To indicate something is to show it; and N, E, W and S are compass points set out, a cryptic description of news.

clue.text: Without help at first, is unable to sing

indicators.note: here means outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: can't means is unable

indicators.note: only the initial letter of the word help is taken

explanation.surface: Someone who can't carry a tune unaided.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Without' is the old sense 'outside': CANT goes around H, the first letter of help.
explanation.definitionFit: To chant is to sing in a repetitive, monotonous way, so it is a kind of singing.

clue.text: They sing in a lot of variety shows, chiefly

indicators.note: a variety of the letters is a different arrangement of them
the chief, or first, letter of the word shows

explanation.surface: Singers who appear in many variety shows.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of variety' rearranges A LOT; 'chiefly' takes S from shows. 'Variety shows' looks like one phrase but is split.
explanation.definitionFit: Altos are singers with the lower female or high male voice, so they are people who sing.

clue.text: A show of pride?

parts.note: a pride is a group of lions, and the male's shaggy ruff is their most impressive display

explanation.surface: An outward display of self-satisfaction or arrogance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'pride' looks like the feeling, but it is the collective noun for lions.
explanation.definitionFit: A pride is a group of big cats, and the male's thick neck hair is its showiest feature.

clue.text: The Dickens Baritone art house showing

indicators.note: the answer is on show within the letters of these words

explanation.surface: A baritone performs Dickens at an art-house cinema.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Dickens' is not the novelist but the intensifier in 'what the dickens?', which means the same as 'what on earth?'.
explanation.definitionFit: In 'what the dickens' the phrase is an intensifier, exactly as in 'what on earth'.

clue.text: Expressed in letters, Cage's last piece, on margins in italic

indicators.note: only the final letter of the composer's name is taken

parts.note: a piece is slang for a gun, such as a pistol

indicators.note: the margins of a word are its outermost letters, first and last

explanation.surface: A tribute to John Cage, the composer, written in italic script.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cage's last' gives E; 'piece' looks musical but is a gun; 'margins in italic' gives IC.
explanation.definitionFit: Epistolic describes things conveyed by correspondence, so it means communicated in letters.

clue.text: Singer, fantastic belter

indicators.note: something fantastic is wild and fanciful, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Praise for a vocalist with a powerful voice.
explanation.definitionFit: A treble is a boy with a high voice who sings in a choir.

clue.text: Leveraged restructuring for Slough?

indicators.note: restructuring rebuilds something in a new form, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A leveraged business reorganisation in Slough, an English commuter town.
explanation.walkthrough: Slough looks like the town west of London, but it is the common noun for a swamp.
explanation.definitionFit: A slough is a swamp or marsh, and the Everglades are a famous marshy region of Florida.

clue.text: Perhaps Amy was a mythical woman, a Greek character in times past

indicators.note: the woman and the Greek letter go inside the era abbreviation

parts.note: BC marks dates before Christ, in times long past
Io is the maiden of Greek myth loved by Zeus and turned into a heifer
pi is a letter of the Greek alphabet

explanation.surface: Speculation on whether a woman named Amy was a figure from Greek myth.
explanation.walkthrough: Amy is the 2015 documentary film about the singer Amy Winehouse.
explanation.definitionFit: Amy is a film about the life of Amy Winehouse, an example of a life-story film.

clue.text: Bach's music? It was sung in church or it was enjoyed in taverns

parts.note: ale is the drink long enjoyed in taverns

explanation.surface: Was Bach's music performed in church, or sung over drinks in the pub?
explanation.definitionFit: A chorale is a Lutheran hymn tune, many harmonised by Bach and sung by congregations.

clue.text: Conflict with British over shortly, retreating unprepared

parts.note: o'er is the shortened poetic form of over

indicators.note: going backwards, so the word is read from right to left

parts.note: raw means untrained or unprepared

explanation.surface: A war report: the British retreating, ill-prepared, with the fight soon over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retreating' reverses RAW to WAR.
explanation.definitionFit: The Boer Wars were conflicts in southern Africa between Britain and the Boer republics.

clue.text: Sing out from the depths: Dylan's heart's in it

indicators.note: the letter is placed within the word just given

parts.note: below means down beneath, in the depths

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

explanation.surface: Bob Dylan singing from deep down, his heart in the song.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heart' takes L, the middle of DYLAN, and 'in it' puts that inside BELOW.
explanation.definitionFit: To bellow is to shout or roar loudly, the same as to sing out.

clue.text: Enlists guys, perhaps Boatman, by name

parts.note: guys are ropes holding a tent or mast steady
Boatman is this puzzle's setter, who refers to themself as I

explanation.surface: A boatman enlists some crewmen.
explanation.walkthrough: Boatman is the setter, so 'perhaps Boatman' is I, the setter speaking.
explanation.definitionFit: To rope someone in is to persuade them to join, which means to enlist them.

clue.text: Two articles covering Mahler's first song

indicators.note: in a down entry the articles sit above the letter, covering it

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
the is the definite article

indicators.note: the initial letter of the composer's name is taken

explanation.surface: Two essays reviewing a Mahler song.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'covering' puts the two articles on top of M, the first letter of Mahler.
explanation.definitionFit: An anthem is a song of praise or a rousing national song.

clue.text: Spice extract unaltered by hard work overwhelming small girl

parts.note: read as UN altered: the two letters of un rearranged

indicators.note: to overwhelm is to engulf, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: toil is hard work
Meg is a short form of the name Margaret

explanation.surface: A spice extract kept pure despite heavy labour that leaves a little girl exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'unaltered' splits as UN altered, the two letters swapped; 'overwhelming' wraps the hard work round the small girl.
explanation.definitionFit: This aromatic oil is distilled from the seed of the nutmeg, a spice.

clue.text: Green at heart? Jealous ego? It could make you ill

parts.note: eco is the prefix for environmentally green

indicators.note: the heart of a word is its middle letter

parts.note: the ego is the self, I

explanation.surface: Is a green-eyed, jealous ego a sickness at heart?
explanation.walkthrough: 'at heart' sits by 'Green' but applies to 'Jealous', giving L.
explanation.definitionFit: E. coli is a gut bacterium, some strains of which cause food poisoning.

clue.text: Sing rap: hold tight!

parts.note: read as 'S in G, rap': the letter S is put inside the letters G plus RAP

explanation.surface: An order to a rapper to hang on.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sing' splits as S in G; with RAP following, the S lands inside GRAP.
explanation.definitionFit: To grasp something is to grip it firmly, so it means hold tight.

clue.text: A crooner's opening with popular number one in concert — they get raspberries!

indicators.note: the opening of the crooner's name is its first letter

parts.note: in means popular or fashionable
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A crooner and a popular hit in concert are given raspberries by the crowd.
explanation.walkthrough: A raspberry is a rude noise of derision, but here it is the fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Acini are the small drupelets that cluster to form a raspberry or blackberry.

clue.text: Jealous man losing love, heading for tragedy that's unexpected

indicators.note: the jealous man loses these letters

parts.note: Othello is Shakespeare's jealous husband
love means nil in tennis, the letter O

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A jealous man loses his love, heading for an unexpected tragedy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing' removes O (love) and T (head of tragedy) from OTHELLO.
explanation.definitionFit: Hello is an exclamation of surprise, as in 'hello, what's this?'.

clue.text: Inconsistencies in Leonardo's work: first half is back to front; second half reportedly so

indicators.text: first half is back to front
indicators.note: the first part of the painting's name is read in reverse

parts.note: the Mona Lisa is Leonardo da Vinci's most famous painting; its first half is Mona

indicators.note: the second part is also turned round, and then only the sound matches

parts.note: the second half, Lisa, turned round reads ASIL

explanation.surface: An art critic finds flaws in Leonardo's painting.
explanation.walkthrough: MONA reversed gives ANOM; LISA reversed gives ASIL, which when said sounds like ALIES.
explanation.definitionFit: Anomalies are things that deviate from the norm, so they are inconsistencies.

clue.text: See 1
Singer, collapsing, to bow out

indicators.note: something collapsing falls apart, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A singer collapses on stage and has to quit.
explanation.definitionFit: To resign is to give up a post, so it means to withdraw or bow out.
